look_here_first: Start with fruit size and leaflet narrowness. Little walnut is the smallest-fruited local walnut: fruits about 1.4–2.3 cm and nuts about 1.1–1.7 cm, with 17–25 narrow leaflets. It is usually a shrub or small tree rather than a massive canopy tree.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays County field collection between Five Mile Dam and Blanco Shoals; Bandera County riparian documentation explicitly lists little walnut; Comal County historical national-champion record near Fischer documents the species.

best_field_traits: shrub or small tree, generally to about 10 m
nut about 1.1–1.7 cm with longitudinal grooves and relatively smooth surfaces between grooves
morphology_keys.comparison_training: J. major has fewer, broader leaflets and larger 2–3.5 cm fruits; J. nigra has much larger 3.5–8 cm fruits and a coarsely warty nut surface.

comparisons.key_distinctions: J. major has fewer, broader leaflets and larger 2–3.5 cm fruits; J. nigra has much larger 3.5–8 cm fruits and a coarsely warty nut surface.

taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO. Flora of North America warns that central Texas intermediates occur among local walnut species; use multiple characters on atypical material.
